exercises.name: Standing Barbell Curl
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: Elbow flexion is the main action; grip and forearm orientation influence assistance from brachialis and brachioradialis.
instructions: Stand or sit with a stable trunk, arms near the sides unless the named variation specifies otherwise, and wrists neutral.
Bend the elbow to bring the resistance toward the shoulder without swinging the torso; lower slowly to the start.
Breathe steadily and keep the movement pain-free.
End the set if technique changes or you cannot lower the resistance under control.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body or using momentum to complete repetitions.
Allowing wrists to bend sharply or joints to move through painful ranges.
Letting shoulders or elbows drift when the exercise calls for a stable arm position.
Using too much resistance and losing control of the lowering phase.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, tingling, or loss of grip; reduce resistance if wrist, elbow, or shoulder discomfort appears.
Use controlled repetitions and avoid sudden jerking or forced end ranges.
Secure benches, bars, cables, bands, and anchors; choose assistance or lighter resistance when needed.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

met_assumption.selection_guidance: Choose and document a MET value appropriate to the exercise and intensity; do not assign a universal value based only on exercise name.

calorie_estimation.rest_periods: Capture rest seconds separately. Do not apply active-work MET over rest; model rest separately only when reporting total session energy.
caveats: This is a population-level estimate, not a measured personal calorie count.
Energy expenditure varies with body mass, effort, tempo, range of motion, training status, and rest.
Do not infer calories from repetitions or external load alone.
Show assumptions and uncertainty; avoid false precision.
calorie_estimation.output_precision: round to no more than whole kcal; consider showing a range when MET assumptions are uncertain.

instructions: Use stable parallel bars or a secure bench and begin with assisted or partial range if bodyweight is too challenging.
Bend the elbows through a comfortable range while keeping the upper arms controlled, then press back to the start without locking forcefully.
Breathe steadily and keep the movement pain-free.
End the set if technique changes or you cannot lower the resistance under control.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body or using momentum to complete repetitions.
Allowing wrists to bend sharply or joints to move through painful ranges.
Letting shoulders or elbows drift when the exercise calls for a stable arm position.
Using too much resistance and losing control of the lowering phase.
safety_cautions: Dips can place substantial demand on the shoulders; use a pain-free depth and skip the movement if the shoulder is uncomfortable.
Stop for sharp pain, numbness, tingling, or loss of grip; reduce resistance if wrist, elbow, or shoulder discomfort appears.
Use controlled repetitions and avoid sudden jerking or forced end ranges.
Secure benches, bars, cables, bands, and anchors; choose assistance or lighter resistance when needed.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

instructions: Use a light resistance first, support the forearm when appropriate, and keep the wrist path controlled.
Perform the named wrist, grip, or forearm action smoothly; keep the rest of the arm steady and release under control.
Breathe steadily and keep the movement pain-free.
End the set if technique changes or you cannot lower the resistance under control.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body or using momentum to complete repetitions.
Allowing wrists to bend sharply or joints to move through painful ranges.
Letting shoulders or elbows drift when the exercise calls for a stable arm position.
Using too much resistance and losing control of the lowering phase.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, tingling, or loss of grip; reduce resistance if wrist, elbow, or shoulder discomfort appears.
Use controlled repetitions and avoid sudden jerking or forced end ranges.
Secure benches, bars, cables, bands, and anchors; choose assistance or lighter resistance when needed.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

calorie_estimation.rest_periods: Capture rest seconds separately. Do not apply active-work MET over rest; model rest separately only when reporting total session energy.

calorie_estimation.output_precision: round to no more than whole kcal; consider showing a range when MET assumptions are uncertain.
